components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 字: a room under the roof.
至 (zhì, arrive) is a loose sound clue for shì; it fits the meaning: where one arrives inside the house.

example.hanzi: 我们在会议室开会。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài huìyìshì kāihuì.
example.english: We're holding a meeting in the meeting room.
example.fact: 室 is mostly a suffix: 教室 (classroom), 办公室 (office), 卧室 (bedroom), 浴室 (bathroom), 室友 (roommate). Apartment ads use it for layout: 两室一厅 means two bedrooms and one living room.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài bàngōngshì gōngzuò.
examples.english: He works in the office.

examples.pinyin: Jiàoshì lǐ méiyǒu rén.
examples.english: There is nobody in the classroom.

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — drink, as in 酒 liquor, 醒 sober.
卒 (zú) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 翠 cuì and 碎 suì.

example.hanzi: 他喝醉了，一直在唱歌。
example.pinyin: Tā hēzuì le, yìzhí zài chànggē.
example.english: He got drunk and kept singing.
example.fact: 醉 is mostly used as 喝醉 (get drunk) or 醉了 (be drunk). It extends to being enraptured: 陶醉 (be fascinated). 醉酒驾驶 is the legal term for drunk driving, and in slang 我醉了 can mean "I give up/I'm speechless".

examples.hanzi: 他昨晚喝醉了，今天头很疼。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuówǎn hēzuì le, jīntiān tóu hěn téng.
examples.english: He got drunk last night and has a headache today.

examples.pinyin: Bié hē le, nǐ yǐjīng zuì le.
examples.english: Stop drinking; you're already drunk.

components.note: 虫 (insect) — insects and small creatures: 蚊, 蛇, 蜜; 蠢 is wriggling insects, then stupid.
春 (chūn) is a near sound match for chǔn.

example.hanzi: 我真蠢，又忘了带钥匙。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhēn chǔn, yòu wàng le dài yàoshi.
example.english: I'm so stupid, I forgot my keys again.
example.fact: 蠢 originally meant wriggling, like insects waking in spring, and that image still appears in 蠢蠢欲动 ("stirring and itching to act"). Today it means stupid, blunter than 笨 (bèn), which suggests clumsy or slow.

examples.pinyin: Bié shuō zhème chǔn de huà.
examples.english: Don't say such stupid things.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān zuò le yí jiàn chǔn shì.
examples.english: I did something stupid yesterday.

components.note: 未 (not yet) — a tree 木 with a new short branch on top, still growing. Compare 末 mò (end/tip), where the top stroke is longer.

example.hanzi: 我对未来很有信心。
example.pinyin: Wǒ duì wèilái hěn yǒu xìnxīn.
example.english: I have a lot of confidence in the future.
example.fact: 未 is a formal "not yet" found in 未来 (future), 未成年 (minor), 未婚 (unmarried) and 未必 (not necessarily). In everyday speech it corresponds to 还没. It is also the eighth Earthly Branch of the zodiac cycle, linked to the sheep.

examples.pinyin: Tā hái wèi huíjiā.
examples.english: He has not come home yet.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wèibì shì zhēn de.
examples.english: This may not necessarily be true.

components.note: 彳 (step, conduct) — 彳 is a step or going, as in 行 and 往; 德 is conduct.
心 (heart) — 心 is the heart — the old 悳 was a straight 直 heart, so upright inner conduct.

example.hanzi: 他是个品德很好的人。
example.pinyin: Tā shì ge pǐndé hěn hǎo de rén.
example.english: He is a person of very good character.
example.fact: 德 is virtue in 道德 (morality) and 品德 (moral character). It is also the short form of Germany, 德国, from 德意志 (Deutsch): 德语 is German, 中德 means China–Germany.

examples.pinyin: Tā xué guo Déyǔ.
examples.english: He has studied German.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子很有礼貌，品德很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi hěn yǒu lǐmào, pǐndé hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This child is very polite and of good character.

meanings: sb with whom one has a close personal relationship

components.note: 禾 (grain) — crops: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 私 was grain held for oneself.
厶 (sī) is the ancient form of 私 itself, meaning private; 公 gōng (public) is its opposite.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 这是我的私人物品,请不要动。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de sīrén wùpǐn, qǐng búyào dòng.
example.english: These are my private belongings, please don't touch them.
example.fact: 私人 pairs with a following noun to mark it as personal or private property — 私人医生 ("private doctor"), 私人时间 ("personal time"). The single character 私 already carries the "private, personal" sense on its own, as in 私立 ("privately run," e.g. of schools), but 私人 is the form used to modify another noun.

examples.hanzi: 我想请私人教练帮我健身。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qǐng sīrén jiàoliàn bāng wǒ jiànshēn.
examples.english: I'd like to hire a personal trainer to help me work out.

examples.hanzi: 这是我的私人电话号码。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de sīrén diànhuà hàomǎ.
examples.english: This is my private phone number.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 某 first named a sour tree fruit; now it means a certain, unnamed one. It sounds out 媒 méi, 煤 méi and 谋 móu.

example.hanzi: 某天，我在街上遇到了老同学。
example.pinyin: Mǒu tiān, wǒ zài jiē shang yùdào le lǎo tóngxué.
example.english: One day I ran into an old classmate on the street.
example.fact: 某 points to an unspecified person or thing: 某人, 某天, 某地. In news and legal texts it replaces a real surname to anonymise: 张某 means "a certain Zhang".

examples.hanzi: 某人给我打了个电话，但我不知道是谁。
examples.pinyin: Mǒu rén gěi wǒ dǎ le gè diànhuà, dàn wǒ bù zhīdào shì shéi.
examples.english: Someone called me, but I don't know who.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài mǒu gè gōngsī gōngzuò guo.
examples.english: I once worked at a certain company.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).

example.hanzi: 我们明天早上八点出发。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān zǎoshang bā diǎn chūfā.
example.english: We're setting off at eight tomorrow morning.
example.fact: 出发 combines 出 ("to go out") with 发 ("to send off, to issue") into the literal image of "sending oneself out" on a journey — the same 发 shows up in 发车 ("a vehicle departs") and 出发点 ("starting point," also used figuratively for a starting premise in an argument).

examples.pinyin: Huǒchē jǐ diǎn chūfā?
examples.english: What time does the train set off?

examples.hanzi: 我们准备好了，可以出发了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhǔnbèi hǎo le, kěyǐ chūfā le.
examples.english: We're ready and can set off.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 伟 is a great person.
韦 (wéi) gives a close sound (wěi); same part in 围 wéi, 违 wéi, 纬 wěi.
大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.

example.hanzi: 他是一位伟大的科学家。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi wěidà de kēxuéjiā.
example.english: He is a great scientist.
example.fact: 伟大 is reserved for genuinely momentous, history-scale greatness — a great leader, a great achievement, a great civilization — and sounds oddly over-the-top applied to something merely very good, a register mismatch that trips up learners; that everyday-compliment job instead falls to 很棒 or 太好了.

examples.pinyin: Tā de mèngxiǎng hěn wěidà.
examples.english: His dream is great.

examples.hanzi: 长城是一项伟大的工程。
examples.pinyin: Chángchéng shì yí xiàng wěidà de gōngchéng.
examples.english: The Great Wall is a great feat of engineering.

components.note: 興 (traditional) — several hands lifting together, so to raise, stir, flourish. 兴 keeps only a few strokes; 高兴 is 'high spirits' and 兴趣 is 'interest'.
田 (field) — traditional 奮 shows a bird 隹 spreading its wings 大 out of a field: bursting into effort.

example.hanzi: 听到这个好消息,她非常兴奋。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège hǎo xiāoxi, tā fēicháng xīngfèn.
example.english: Hearing this good news, she was extremely excited.
example.fact: 兴奋 describes a heightened, almost physiological state of excitement — strong enough that 兴奋剂 (literally "excitement agent") is the standard Chinese term for a stimulant or performance-enhancing drug, a more clinical use of the same root than the everyday "excited" sense suggests.

examples.hanzi: 明天去旅行，孩子们都很兴奋。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān qù lǚxíng, háizimen dōu hěn xīngfèn.
examples.english: The children are all excited about the trip tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 他兴奋得一晚上没睡着。
examples.pinyin: Tā xīngfèn de yì wǎnshang méi shuìzháo.
examples.english: He was so excited that he couldn't sleep all night.

components.note: 见 (see) — seeing and vision: 看, 现, 视, 览; 观 is to watch. 又 only stands in for the old sound part 雚 (guàn).
人 (person) — three persons 人人人: a crowd. Also in 观众 audience, 大众 the public.

example.hanzi: 电影结束后,观众都站起来鼓掌。
example.pinyin: Diànyǐng jiéshù hòu, guānzhòng dōu zhàn qǐlai gǔzhǎng.
example.english: After the movie ended, the audience all stood up and applauded.
example.fact: 观众 literally combines 观 ("to watch, observe") with 众 ("crowd, multitude") into "watching crowd." The same 众 appears in 群众 ("the masses") and 大众 ("the public"), a recurring building block for words describing groups of people.

examples.hanzi: 体育场里有三万名观众。
examples.pinyin: Tǐyùchǎng lǐ yǒu sān wàn míng guānzhòng.
examples.english: There are thirty thousand spectators in the stadium.

examples.hanzi: 观众们对这个节目很满意。
examples.pinyin: Guānzhòngmen duì zhè ge jiémù hěn mǎnyì.
examples.english: The audience is very satisfied with this show.

components.note: 自 (nose) + 犬 (dog) — a dog's nose smells; 臭 originally meant smell, now stink, as in 臭味.

example.hanzi: 这双袜子好臭！
example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng wàzi hǎo chòu!
example.english: These socks stink!
example.fact: 臭 is smelly and also used for contempt: 臭美 (conceited), 臭脾气 (bad temper). 臭豆腐 (stinky tofu) is a beloved street food, and the character's original reading xiù ("smell") survives only in 乳臭未干 (still wet behind the ears).

examples.hanzi: 垃圾桶太臭了，快倒掉吧。
examples.pinyin: Lājītǒng tài chòu le, kuài dàodiào ba.
examples.english: The trash can stinks; empty it quickly.

examples.hanzi: 这个臭豆腐闻起来很臭，吃起来很香。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chòudòufu wén qǐlái hěn chòu, chī qǐlái hěn xiāng.
examples.english: This stinky tofu smells bad but tastes good.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 达 is to get through to, to reach.
大 (dà) is only a loose stand-in for the old sound part, so treat it as a rough clue for dá.

example.hanzi: 火车明天上午到达北京。
example.pinyin: Huǒchē míngtiān shàngwǔ dàodá Běijīng.
example.english: The train arrives in Beijing tomorrow morning.
example.fact: 达 is a bound verb, mostly in 到达 (arrive), 达到 (attain: 达到目标), 发达 (developed) and 表达 (express). In writing it also has the sense of reaching a total, as in 达三十人.

examples.hanzi: 他的汉语已经达到了很高的水平。
examples.pinyin: Tā de Hànyǔ yǐjīng dádào le hěn gāo de shuǐpíng.
examples.english: His Chinese has reached a high level.

examples.hanzi: 他想不出合适的话来表达自己。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng bu chū héshì de huà lái biǎodá zìjǐ.
examples.english: He couldn't think of the right words to express himself.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
人 (person) — one person following another: 从 means to follow, then "from".

example.hanzi: 自从上大学以后,我很少回家。
example.pinyin: Zìcóng shàng dàxué yǐhòu, wǒ hěn shǎo huí jiā.
example.english: Since starting university, I've rarely gone home.
example.fact: 自从 almost always sets up a time-clause that gets closed out later by 以后 or 就 ("自从...以后, ..." / "自从...,就..."), marking a change that began at a point in the past and continues into the present — dropping the second half can leave the sentence feeling grammatically unfinished to a native ear.

examples.hanzi: 自从搬家以后，我睡得更好了。
examples.pinyin: Zìcóng bānjiā yǐhòu, wǒ shuì de gèng hǎo le.
examples.english: Since moving house, I've been sleeping better.

examples.hanzi: 自从认识你，我的生活变了。
examples.pinyin: Zìcóng rènshi nǐ, wǒ de shēnghuó biàn le.
examples.english: Ever since I met you, my life has changed.

components.note: 钅 (metal, simplified 金) — metals, as in 钱, 铁, 错: a bell is cast metal.
中 (zhōng) gives the exact sound; 中 also means middle.

example.hanzi: 墙上的钟坏了。
example.pinyin: Qiáng shang de zhōng huài le.
example.english: The clock on the wall is broken.
example.fact: 钟 is a clock or a bell, and in time expressions it marks the hour: 三点钟 (three o'clock), 一个钟头 (an hour), 分钟 (minute). The simplified form merges the old, separate 鍾 and 鐘.

examples.pinyin: Xiànzài shì sān diǎn zhōng.
examples.english: It is three o'clock now.

examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān pǎobù bàn gè zhōngtóu.
examples.english: He jogs for half an hour every day.

components.note: 子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.
弓 (bow) — bows and tension: 张 stretch, 引 draw, 弯 bend; 弹 is to shoot or spring, and a bullet.
单 (dān) is a loose clue for dàn/tán; compare 禅 chán and 蝉 chán.

example.hanzi: 他的枪里已经没有子弹了。
example.pinyin: Tā de qiāng lǐ yǐjīng méiyǒu zǐdàn le.
example.english: There are no more bullets left in his gun.
example.fact: 弹 is a heteronym: read dàn it means a small round projectile (子弹 "bullet," 炸弹 "bomb"), but read tán it means "to pluck, to play (a string instrument)" as in 弹钢琴 ("to play the piano") — the same character, two completely different pronunciations and meanings depending on what's attached to it.

examples.hanzi: 这颗子弹是从哪里来的？
examples.pinyin: Zhè kē zǐdàn shì cóng nǎlǐ lái de?
examples.english: Where did this bullet come from?

examples.hanzi: 警察在现场找到了几颗子弹。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài xiànchǎng zhǎodàole jǐ kē zǐdàn.
examples.english: The police found several bullets at the scene.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; trash is thrown onto the ground.
立 (lì) is only a loose sound hint for lā.
土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; trash is thrown onto the ground.
及 (jí) is a near sound match (jī); same part in 吸 xī, 级 jí, 极 jí.

example.hanzi: 请把垃圾扔进垃圾桶。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ lājī rēng jìn lājītǒng.
example.english: Please throw the trash into the trash can.
example.fact: Mainland Mandarin says lājī, but Taiwan Mandarin traditionally pronounces the very same two characters lèsè — a rare case where two major regional standards diverge sharply enough in pronunciation that the word can sound almost unrelated despite being written identically.

examples.pinyin: Jiē shang yǒu hěn duō lājī.
examples.english: There is a lot of trash on the street.

examples.hanzi: 这是垃圾食品，少吃一点。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì lājī shípǐn, shǎo chī yìdiǎn.
examples.english: This is junk food, so eat less of it.

components.note: 又 (hand) — the bottom-right part and radical, a hand. Dictionary story: the 'smaller (小) brother' of the family; used for a father's younger brother, as in 叔叔.
上 (up) — the top left part, combined with 小 (small) to form the left side of 叔. Memory aid: the small one coming up behind Dad is 'uncle'.
又 (hand) — the bottom-right part and radical, a hand. Dictionary story: the 'smaller (小) brother' of the family; used for a father's younger brother, as in 叔叔.
上 (up) — the top left part, combined with 小 (small) to form the left side of 叔. Memory aid: the small one coming up behind Dad is 'uncle'.

example.hanzi: 那个叔叔在公园里遛狗。
example.pinyin: Nàge shūshu zài gōngyuán lǐ liù gǒu.
example.english: That man is walking his dog in the park.
example.fact: Beyond its precise kinship meaning ("father's younger brother"), 叔叔 also doubles as a polite, generic way for a child to address or refer to an unrelated adult man roughly a parent's age — parallel to how 阿姨 ("auntie") works for women — a common way Chinese kinship terms extend outward into everyday social titles.

examples.hanzi: 叔叔明天来我们家吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Shūshu míngtiān lái wǒmen jiā chīfàn.
examples.english: My uncle is coming to our house for dinner tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 叔叔送了我一个新书包。
examples.pinyin: Shūshu sòngle wǒ yí ge xīn shūbāo.
examples.english: Uncle gave me a new school bag.

components.note: 田 (field) — a field above 力 (strength): a man is one who works the fields with strength.
朋 (friend) — oldest form shows two strings of cowrie shells (old money) side by side; they paired up and came to mean companions.
又 (hand) — two hands 又 stacked: hands joined in friendship.

example.hanzi: 她带男朋友回家见父母。
example.pinyin: Tā dài nánpéngyou huí jiā jiàn fùmǔ.
example.english: She brought her boyfriend home to meet her parents.
example.fact: 男朋友 mirrors 女朋友 (also in this deck) exactly, swapping only the gender character 男 for 女 in front of the shared root 朋友 ("friend") — a simple, symmetric pattern Mandarin reuses across many gendered pairs, like 男生/女生 ("male/female student") and 男老师/女老师 ("male/female teacher").

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de nánpéngyou hěn huì zuòfàn.
examples.english: My boyfriend is a good cook.

examples.hanzi: 她和男朋友一起去旅行了。
examples.pinyin: Tā hé nánpéngyou yìqǐ qù lǚxíng le.
examples.english: She went traveling with her boyfriend.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — marks sickness and pain, as in 病, 痛, 疗; 疼 is to ache.
冬 (dōng) hints at the sound: 疼 téng is close.

example.hanzi: 我的头很疼。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de tóu hěn téng.
example.english: My head hurts.
example.fact: 疼 is the everyday word for pain, more colloquial than 痛 (tòng), which is more formal or sharper. It also means to dote on: 妈妈很疼孩子 ("Mom adores her child"), 疼爱.

examples.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ hěn téng, zǒubuliǎo lù.
examples.english: His leg hurts, so he can't walk.

examples.pinyin: Nǎinai zuì téng tā de sūnzi.
examples.english: Grandma dotes on her grandson most.

components.note: 龶 (plant-like top) — dictionary reads the top as 'a poisonous plant'. Memory aid: a plant growing on top of a mother (母) is something you must not eat.
母 (mǔ, mother) — the bottom part and radical. Sound clue is lost today (毒 is dú); use it as a visual memory aid, as in 母亲.
口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 贩卖毒品是严重的犯罪行为。
example.pinyin: Fànmài dúpǐn shì yánzhòng de fànzuì xíngwéi.
example.english: Selling drugs is a serious crime.
example.fact: 毒品 narrows the broader character 毒 ("poison, toxic") down specifically to illegal narcotics by adding 品 ("product, item"). The same 品 turns other roots into product categories, like 食品 ("food product") or 商品 ("merchandise") — a recurring word-formation slot for "a category of goods."

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào yuǎnlí dúpǐn.
examples.english: We should stay away from drugs.

examples.hanzi: 学校每年都会讲解毒品的危害。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào měi nián dōu huì jiǎngjiě dúpǐn de wēihài.
examples.english: The school explains the dangers of drugs every year.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — ⺮ is bamboo, as in 笔, 筷, 箱; slips of bamboo were written on, so 签 is a slip or to sign.
佥 (qiān) — same sound — 签 is qiān; 佥 also sounds out 检 jiǎn and 脸 liǎn.

example.hanzi: 请在这里签名。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ qiānmíng.
example.english: Please sign your name here.
example.fact: 签 is to sign or put a signature to a document: 签名, 签字, 签证 (visa), 签约 (sign a contract). It is also a divination stick drawn at temples: 抽签 (draw lots). 牙签 is a toothpick.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiān qiānzì, zài ná zhèngjiàn.
examples.english: Please sign first, then take your ID.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yǐjīng qiān le hétong.
examples.english: We have already signed the contract.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
必 (bì) is a sound clue for 秘 mì, 密 mì and 蜜 mì: the same series, with only the initial changing.

example.hanzi: 你不必担心我,我可以照顾自己。
example.pinyin: Nǐ búbì dānxīn wǒ, wǒ kěyǐ zhàogù zìjǐ.
example.english: You don't need to worry about me, I can take care of myself.
example.fact: 不必 is a more formal, compact alternative to 不需要 ("don't need to") — both mean "there's no need to," but 不必 fits into a single beat before the verb, so it turns up constantly in polite reassurances like 不必客气 ("no need to be so polite," a formal cousin of 不用谢).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ búbì zháojí, mànmàn lái.
examples.english: You don't need to rush, take your time.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì búbì gàosu tā.
examples.english: There's no need to tell him about this.

components.note: 又 (hand) — a hand pushing against a cliff 厂: turning back, opposite. Sound series: 饭 fàn, 板 bǎn, 版 bǎn, 返 fǎn.
寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.

example.hanzi: 很多人反对这个新规定。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō rén fǎnduì zhège xīn guīdìng.
example.english: Many people oppose this new regulation.
example.fact: 反对 is built from 反 ("opposite, to turn against") plus 对 ("correct, to face") — literally "to turn against what's correct." Its direct antonym 赞成 ("to approve, to support") is the word most often taught right alongside it, forming one of Mandarin's cleanest opposite pairs.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ fǎnduì zhè ge jìhuà.
examples.english: I oppose this plan.

examples.hanzi: 爸爸反对我一个人去旅行。
examples.pinyin: Bàba fǎnduì wǒ yí ge rén qù lǚxíng.
examples.english: Dad objects to me traveling alone.

meanings: measure word for small round things

components.note: 页 (head) — head-shaped things; 颗 is a measure word for small round things like grains, pearls and beads, as in 一颗星.
果 (guǒ) — loose sound hint (kē vs guǒ); 果 also means fruit, a round thing.

example.hanzi: 天上有很多颗星星。
example.pinyin: Tiānshang yǒu hěn duō kē xīngxing.
example.english: There are a lot of stars in the sky.
example.fact: 颗 counts small, round or grain-like things: 一颗星, 一颗糖, 一颗牙, 一颗心 (a heart). It is a bit more vivid or literary than 个, and the stricter 粒 is for tiny grains such as rice.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ chīle yì kē táng.
examples.english: I ate a piece of candy.

examples.pinyin: Zhè kē yá yǒudiǎn téng.
examples.english: This tooth hurts a bit.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 停 is a person stopping.
亭 (tíng) sounds exactly like 停; same part in 婷 tíng.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 车突然停下了。
example.pinyin: Chē tūrán tíng xià le.
example.english: The car suddenly stopped.
example.fact: 停下 attaches the directional complement 下 ("down") to the plain verb 停 ("to stop") to emphasize a full, physical halt in motion — it contrasts with the more formal, abstract 停止, which is used for stopping an activity or process rather than a moving object.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài ménkǒu tíngxià.
examples.english: Please stop at the door.

examples.hanzi: 听到有人叫他，他停下了脚步。
examples.pinyin: Tīngdào yǒu rén jiào tā, tā tíngxiàle jiǎobù.
examples.english: Hearing someone call him, he stopped walking.

components.note: 肉 — a picture of a slab of meat with its grain lines; as a left-hand radical it shrinks to ⺼ in 脸, 腿, 肌.

example.hanzi: 我不吃肉，只吃菜。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bù chī ròu, zhǐ chī cài.
example.english: I don't eat meat, only vegetables.
example.fact: Unqualified 肉 usually means pork in China (猪肉), with other meats named explicitly: 牛肉, 羊肉, 鸡肉. 肉 is also fruit flesh (果肉) and, as the radical ⺼, shows up in body parts such as 脚 and 肝.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng chī ròu, bù xiǎng chī qīngcài.
examples.english: I want to eat meat, not vegetables.

examples.pinyin: Tā de tuǐ shang méiyǒu ròu, hěn shòu.
examples.english: His legs have no flesh; he is very thin.

meanings: to test (a person's skill in a particular area)

components.note: 氵 (water radical, 三点水) — water: 河, 深, 浅; 测 was measuring the depth of water.
则 (zé) is close to cè; same part in 侧 cè and 厕 cè.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and language: 说 say, 请 ask, 读 read; testing often involves questions.
式 (shì) sounds exactly like 试 — a reliable sound clue.

example.hanzi: 这个软件还在测试阶段。
example.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn hái zài cèshì jiēduàn.
example.english: This software is still in the testing phase.
example.fact: 测试 leans technical and is the standard word for testing software, machinery, or a hypothesis, while testing a person's classroom knowledge more often reaches for 测验 or the everyday 考试 ("exam") — three overlapping "test" words roughly sorted by what's actually being tested.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān yǒu yí ge Hànyǔ cèshì.
examples.english: There is a Chinese test tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 工程师正在测试新手机。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchéngshī zhèngzài cèshì xīn shǒujī.
examples.english: The engineer is testing the new phone.

components.note: 米 (rice) — refined grain gives the idea of essence and the best part, hence 精 fine, spirit (精神).
青 (qīng) is a near sound match (-ing); the series 青 清 请 情 晴 静 helps recall jīng.
彡 (hair strokes, decoration) — patterns and appearance: 形 shape, 影 shadow, 须 beard; 彩 is colorful decoration.
采 (cǎi) sounds exactly like 彩; also in 菜 cài and 踩 cǎi.

example.hanzi: 这场比赛真精彩!
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng bǐsài zhēn jīngcǎi!
example.english: This match was truly brilliant!
example.fact: 精彩 praises the quality of a performance, show, speech, or match — vivid, skillful, and engaging — rather than a person's character. A movie, a goal, or a talk can be 精彩, but calling a person 精彩 sounds like an odd, non-standard compliment; 精彩 sticks to describing performances and moments.

examples.pinyin: Tā de biǎoyǎn hěn jīngcǎi.
examples.english: Her performance is wonderful.

examples.hanzi: 他讲了一个精彩的故事。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎngle yí ge jīngcǎi de gùshi.
examples.english: He told a wonderful story.

components.note: 今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.

example.hanzi: 这条项链是金做的。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo xiàngliàn shì jīn zuò de.
example.english: This necklace is made of gold.
example.fact: 金 is gold and, more broadly, metal and money: 现金 (cash), 奖金 (bonus), 金钱. It is one of the Five Elements (金木水火土), and as a surname it is also how Korean Kim is written.

examples.pinyin: Jīnzi hěn guì.
examples.english: Gold is very expensive.

examples.pinyin: Tā dé le yí kuài jīnpái.
examples.english: He won a gold medal.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings and thoughts, as in 想, 思, 急; 感 is to feel or be moved.
咸 (xián) is a loose sound clue for gǎn; 咸 also sounds out 喊 hǎn and 减 jiǎn.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 他们之间的感情很深。
example.pinyin: Tāmen zhījiān de gǎnqíng hěn shēn.
example.english: The bond between them is deep.
example.fact: 感情 and 感觉 are frequently confused by learners since English “feelings” covers both: 感情 names an emotional bond or sentiment, often between people (谈感情, “to nurture a relationship”), while 感觉 covers a momentary sensory impression or hunch (一种奇怪的感觉, “a strange feeling”).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé tā méiyǒu gǎnqíng le.
examples.english: She and I no longer have feelings for each other.

examples.hanzi: 他对家乡有很深的感情。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì jiāxiāng yǒu hěn shēn de gǎnqíng.
examples.english: He has deep feelings for his hometown.

components.note: 月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 住; 候 means to wait for someone.
侯 (hóu) is a close sound clue for hòu; it also gives 猴 hóu monkey and 喉 hóu throat.

example.hanzi: 我有时候会忘记吃早饭。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yǒushíhou huì wàngjì chī zǎofàn.
example.english: Sometimes I forget to eat breakfast.
example.fact: 有时候 is literally “there are times [when]” — 有 (“to have, there is”) plus 时候 (“time, moment”) — and is very often doubled as 有时候...有时候... to contrast two alternating situations, matching English “sometimes...sometimes...”

examples.hanzi: 有时候我想一个人待着。
examples.pinyin: Yǒu shíhou wǒ xiǎng yí ge rén dāizhe.
examples.english: Sometimes I want to be alone.

examples.hanzi: 你有时候会不会觉得很累？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shíhou huì bu huì juéde hěn lèi?
examples.english: Do you sometimes feel very tired?

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — clothes and wrapping: 装, 被, 衬; 袭 is to attack suddenly, an old sense of "cover over". 龙 is only a loose sound clue.
凵 (open box) — the bottom part and dictionary radical. 击 simplifies 擊, whose 手 (hand) hinted at striking. Memory aid: a blow landing in a hollow.

example.hanzi: 敌军在夜里发动了突然袭击。
example.pinyin: Díjūn zài yèli fādòng le tūrán xíjī.
example.english: The enemy troops launched a sudden attack at night.
example.fact: 袭's traditional form is linked to layered ceremonial robes and, by extension, to “inheriting, carrying on” a pattern — a sense that still surfaces in 沿袭 (“to carry on a tradition”) and 抄袭 (“to plagiarize,” literally “to copy and carry on”) — while 袭击 itself narrowed long ago to the “sudden raid, ambush” sense seen here.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎozhèn zuótiān zāodàole xíjī.
examples.english: The town was attacked yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 一只狗突然袭击了路过的人。
examples.pinyin: Yì zhī gǒu tūrán xíjīle lùguò de rén.
examples.english: A dog suddenly attacked a passerby.

components.note: 氵 (water) — water and flow, as in 河, 海, 清: 演 first meant a long flowing stream, then spreading out and performing.
寅 (yín) is a close sound clue for yǎn.
凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.

example.hanzi: 今晚的演出非常精彩。
example.pinyin: Jīnwǎn de yǎnchū fēicháng jīngcǎi.
example.english: Tonight's performance was excellent.
example.fact: 演 alone already means “to perform, to act” (as in 表演), and 出 contributes a sense of “coming out, appearing” — together 演出 paints the fairly literal image of a performance “coming out” before an audience.

examples.hanzi: 他在这部电视剧里演出主角。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhè bù diànshìjù lǐ yǎnchū zhǔjué.
examples.english: He plays the lead role in this TV drama.

examples.hanzi: 这个剧团明天在城里演出。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jùtuán míngtiān zài chéng lǐ yǎnchū.
examples.english: This theater troupe performs in the city tomorrow.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 她把一生都献给了教育事业。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ yìshēng dōu xiàngěi le jiàoyù shìyè.
example.english: She dedicated her whole life to education.
example.fact: 一生 is the more literary, written counterpart to the everyday spoken synonym 一辈子 (yíbèizi) — both mean “a whole lifetime,” but 一生 shows up far more in writing and formal speech, while 一辈子 dominates casual conversation.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng hé nǐ guò yìshēng.
examples.english: I want to spend my whole life with you.

examples.hanzi: 这是他一生中最难忘的一天。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tā yìshēng zhōng zuì nánwàng de yì tiān.
examples.english: This was the most unforgettable day of his life.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地 earth, 坐 sit; 在 is "to be at a place".
才 (cái) is a close sound clue for zài; 才 also appears in 材 cái.
乎 (hū) — as a sound part it gives hū to 呼 (call out, breathe out), so 呼 and 乎 sound the same.

example.hanzi: 我一点儿都不在乎结果。
example.pinyin: Wǒ yìdiǎnr dōu bú zàihu jiéguǒ.
example.english: I don't care about the result at all.
example.fact: 不在乎 attaches directly to a noun or clause with no preposition needed (不在乎钱, “doesn't care about money”; 不在乎别人怎么说, “doesn't care what others say”) — a contrast with English “to care about,” which always needs “about” before its object.

examples.hanzi: 别人怎么说，我都不在乎。
examples.pinyin: Biéren zěnme shuō, wǒ dōu bú zàihu.
examples.english: I don't care what others say.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bú zàihu wǒ de gǎnshòu ma?
examples.english: Don't you care about my feelings?

components.note: 月 (moon) — in the oldest form the sun rises in the grass while the moon is still up: early morning. A court audience was held at dawn, hence cháo for court and dynasty.

example.hanzi: 请一直朝前走。
example.pinyin: Qǐng yìzhí cháo qián zǒu.
example.english: Please keep walking straight ahead.
example.fact: 朝 as cháo means "towards" and "dynasty": 朝向, 唐朝, 朝代. The older sense "morning" is read zhāo, as in 朝气蓬勃 (full of vitality) — a classic two-reading character.

examples.pinyin: Chuānghu cháo nán, hěn liàng.
examples.english: The window faces south and is bright.

examples.pinyin: Tā cháo wǒ xiàole xiào.
examples.english: He smiled at me.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 吸, 叫, 喊; 呼 is to breathe out or call.
乎 (hū) sounds exactly like 呼.
口 (mouth) — breath and speech: 呼, 吃, 喝; 吸 is to breathe in.
及 (jí) is a loose sound hint for xī; same part in 级 jí and 极 jí.

example.hanzi: 深呼吸可以帮助你放松。
example.pinyin: Shēn hūxī kěyǐ bāngzhù nǐ fàngsōng.
example.english: Deep breathing can help you relax.
example.fact: 呼 and 吸 individually mean “to exhale” and “to inhale” — 呼吸 fuses two opposite-direction breathing actions into one word for “to breathe,” a compounding pattern (pairing complementary opposites) also seen in words like 买卖 (“buy-sell,” meaning “business, trade”).

examples.hanzi: 他呼吸很困难，需要看医生。
examples.pinyin: Tā hūxī hěn kùnnan, xūyào kàn yīshēng.
examples.english: He is having difficulty breathing and needs to see a doctor.

examples.hanzi: 山上的空气好，你可以多呼吸一下。
examples.pinyin: Shān shàng de kōngqì hǎo, nǐ kěyǐ duō hūxī yíxià.
examples.english: The air on the mountain is good, so breathe in more.

components.note: 日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.
日 (sun) — sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear, 时 time; stars are points of light.
生 (shēng) is a loose sound hint for xīng (-ng ending); also in 性 xìng, 姓 xìng.

example.hanzi: 她是一位很受欢迎的电影明星。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi hěn shòu huānyíng de diànyǐng míngxīng.
example.english: She is a very popular movie star.
example.fact: 明星 literally means “bright star” (明 “bright” + 星 “star”) — the image of a celebrity as a bright, shining star in the sky lines up almost exactly with the same metaphor in English “star.”

examples.hanzi: 我想见我最喜欢的明星。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng jiàn wǒ zuì xǐhuan de míngxīng.
examples.english: I want to meet my favorite star.

examples.hanzi: 这位明星经常去帮助孩子们。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi míngxīng jīngcháng qù bāngzhù háizimen.
examples.english: This celebrity often goes to help children.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.

example.hanzi: 我的手机没电了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī méi diàn le.
example.english: My phone is out of battery.
example.fact: 机 is a bound word for machines: 手机 (mobile phone), 飞机 (plane), 洗衣机 (washing machine), 机场 (airport). It also means opportunity: 机会, and 机器 is machine.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen qù jīchǎng zuò fēijī.
examples.english: We're going to the airport to take a plane.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个好机会，别错过。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè hǎo jīhuì, bié cuòguò.
examples.english: This is a good opportunity; don't miss it.

components.note: 土 (earth) — ground and land: 地, 场, 块; city walls were made of earth.
成 (chéng) sounds exactly like 城; also in 诚 chéng and 盛 chéng.

example.hanzi: 我住在城里，不住在乡下。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài chéng lǐ, bú zhù zài xiāngxia.
example.english: I live in the city, not in the countryside.
example.fact: 城 originally meant the city wall, which was the defining feature of a city. 城市 is a city, 城里 means "in town" (versus 乡下), 长城 is the Great Wall, and 封城 means to lock a city down.

examples.pinyin: Tāmen zhù zài zhè zuò chéng lǐ.
examples.english: They live in this city.

examples.hanzi: 这座老城有一千年的历史。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò lǎochéng yǒu yì qiān nián de lìshǐ.
examples.english: This old town has a history of a thousand years.

components.note: 走 (run, walk) — movement: 起 rise, 越 cross, 赶 hurry, 趣; 超 is to jump over, surpass.
召 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 招 zhāo, 绍 shào, 照 zhào.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 给; 级 first meant the order of threads, then rank.
及 (jí) sounds exactly like 级; also 极 jí, 吸 xī.

example.hanzi: 这部电影超级好看!
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng chāojí hǎokàn!
example.english: This movie is super good!
example.fact: 超 (“to exceed, surpass”) plus 级 (“grade, level”) literally means “exceeding the normal grade” — a transparent compositional root that made 超级 a natural fit both for coining terms like 超级市场 (“supermarket”) and, in casual speech, for use as a standalone intensifying prefix before an adjective (超级好, “super good”), echoing English “super-.”

examples.pinyin: Zhège shǒujī chāojí hǎoyòng.
examples.english: This phone is super easy to use.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi chāojí yīngxióng.
examples.english: He is a superhero.

components.note: 火 (fire) — the bottom part, as in 灯 lamp and 炎 flame. The dictionary lists fire as the hint: a spirit like a flickering flame, as in 灵魂.
彐 (snout) — the top part, a stroke group as in 当 and 归. 灵 simplifies 靈, so this shape is not a sound clue. Memory aid: a hand over a flame, feeling a spirit.
鬼 (ghost) — spirits and the unseen: 魔 demon, 魅 charm, 魄 spirit; 魂 is the soul.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for hún.

example.hanzi: 音乐是这部电影的灵魂。
example.pinyin: Yīnyuè shì zhè bù diànyǐng de línghún.
example.english: Music is the soul of this film.
example.fact: 灵 and 魂 are near-synonyms that both independently can mean “spirit, soul” (灵 tied to ritual and the numinous, 魂 tied to a person's spirit surviving after death) — reinforcing two overlapping “spirit” characters into one word is the same doubling strategy behind common words like 喜欢 (“to like”) and 应该 (“should”).

examples.pinyin: Tā de huà lǐ yǒu línghún.
examples.english: There is soul in his paintings.

examples.hanzi: 人们相信死后灵魂还会存在。
examples.pinyin: Rénmen xiāngxìn sǐ hòu línghún hái huì cúnzài.
examples.english: People believe the soul continues to exist after death.

components.note: 石 (stone) — stones and hard things: 研, 码, 砖; 破 is to smash or break.
皮 (pí) is a loose sound clue; same series 坡 pō, 披 pī, 波 bō.
土 (earth) — soil and land: 地, 场, 块; 坏 first meant to collapse, as of a wall of earth.
不 (bù) is only a stand-in for the old sound part 褱 (huái); a loose clue for huài.

example.hanzi: 大雨破坏了我们的旅行计划。
example.pinyin: Dàyǔ pòhuài le wǒmen de lǚxíng jìhuà.
example.english: The heavy rain ruined our travel plans.
example.fact: 破坏 extends easily from physical destruction (破坏建筑, “destroy a building”) to abstract damage (破坏关系, “damage a relationship”; 破坏计划, “ruin a plan”) — a metaphorical extension from physical breaking to abstract harm that mirrors how English “wreck” or “ruin” work.

examples.pinyin: Bié pòhuài gōngyuán lǐ de huā.
examples.english: Don't damage the flowers in the park.

examples.hanzi: 吵架会破坏朋友之间的感情。
examples.pinyin: Chǎojià huì pòhuài péngyou zhījiān de gǎnqíng.
examples.english: Arguing damages the friendship between friends.

components.note: 只 (only; measure word) — two old characters merged: 隻 zhī "a single (bird), measure word" and 只 zhǐ "only".
一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.

example.hanzi: 他只不过是个孩子,别太严格。
example.pinyin: Tā zhǐbuguò shì ge háizi, bié tài yángé.
example.english: He's just a child, don't be too strict.
example.fact: 只不过 stacks three separate limiting pieces — 只 (“only”), 不 (“not”), 过 (“exceed”) — into one phrase that reads almost like “only not exceeding,” reinforcing a single idea of “merely, no more than” through triple repetition rather than any one character doing the job alone.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐ bu guò shì ge xiǎo wèntí.
examples.english: This is merely a small problem.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ bu guò xiǎng bāngbang nǐ.
examples.english: I only wanted to help you.

components.note: 户 (door) — doors and houses, as in 所 and 扇: a room with a door.
方 (fāng) is a close sound clue for fáng; 方 also sounds out 放 fàng and 访 fǎng.

example.hanzi: 我们刚买了一套房。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen gāng mǎi le yí tào fáng.
example.english: We just bought an apartment.
example.fact: 房 is a house or room, counted for apartments with 套 (一套房). It forms 房子 (house), 房间 (room), 厨房 (kitchen), 房租 (rent) and 房东 (landlord).

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiān fáng hěn dà, yě hěn míngliàng.
examples.english: This room is big and bright.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zū fáng, bù mǎi fáng.
examples.english: We want to rent a place rather than buy one.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings: 怕, 情, 快; 愉 is a happy heart.
俞 (yú) sounds exactly like 愉; also in 偷 tōu and 输 shū.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 怕, 忙, 情: a quick, glad heart.
夬 (guài) is a close sound clue for kuài; 夬 also in 块 kuài, 筷 kuài and 决 jué.

example.hanzi: 祝你旅途愉快!
example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ lǚtú yúkuài!
example.english: Wishing you a pleasant journey!
example.fact: 愉快 is the go-to word for polite, formal well-wishing (祝你...愉快, as in 生日愉快 “happy birthday” or 新年愉快 “happy new year”) — for describing one's own everyday mood in casual speech, 高兴 or 开心 is far more common.

examples.pinyin: Zhù dàjiā xīnnián yúkuài!
examples.english: Wishing everyone a happy new year!

examples.hanzi: 我们昨天度过了一个愉快的周末。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuótiān dùguòle yí ge yúkuài de zhōumò.
examples.english: We had a pleasant weekend yesterday.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire and heat: 灯, 烧, 炸, 热; 爆 is to burst in flames.
暴 (bào) sounds exactly like 爆, and means violent.
火 (fire) — fire and heat: 灯, 烧, 爆; 炸 is to explode or to fry.
乍 (zhà) sounds exactly like 炸; also in 诈 zhà, 作 zuò, 昨 zuó.

example.hanzi: 工厂里发生了一次严重的爆炸。
example.pinyin: Gōngchǎng lǐ fāshēng le yí cì yánzhòng de bàozhà.
example.english: A serious explosion occurred at the factory.
example.fact: 爆 and 炸 are near-synonymous “explode” verbs reinforced together in 爆炸, but each also branches off on its own into an everyday food word — 爆 shows up in 爆米花 (“popcorn,” literally “exploded rice flower”) while 炸 shows up in 炸鸡 (“fried chicken”), since deep-frying and exploding share the same sudden burst of heat.

examples.hanzi: 爆竹一爆炸，孩子们就笑了。
examples.pinyin: Bàozhú yí bàozhà, háizimen jiù xiào le.
examples.english: As soon as the firecracker exploded, the kids laughed.

examples.hanzi: 新闻说，那里发生了爆炸。
examples.pinyin: Xīnwén shuō, nàlǐ fāshēngle bàozhà.
examples.english: The news said an explosion happened there.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 迟 is slow going, late.
尺 (chǐ) is a close sound match, tone differs.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 今天早上我又迟到了。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān zǎoshang wǒ yòu chídào le.
example.english: I was late again this morning.
example.fact: 迟到 is a resultative compound — 迟 (“late, slow”) describing the manner, 到 (“to arrive”) naming the result — fusing manner and outcome into one word, the same pattern behind 听到 (“to hear,” literally “listen and succeed”) and 看到 (“to see”).

examples.pinyin: Shàngkè búyào chídào.
examples.english: Don't be late for class.

examples.hanzi: 对不起，我迟到了十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ chídàole shí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: Sorry, I was ten minutes late.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 帽, 帮: a belt of cloth with pieces hanging from it.
走 (walk, run) — a person with swinging arms above a foot 止. As a radical it marks movement: 起, 越, 超, 趣.

example.hanzi: 请把垃圾带走。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ lājī dàizǒu.
example.english: Please take the trash away.
example.fact: 带走 pairs 带 (“to bring along”) with the directional complement 走 (“to leave, go away”) to mark an item as carried off and away from here, contrasting with 带来 (“to bring here,” 来 = “to come”) — one of many verb pairs built on the same 来/走 “toward/away” opposition.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ bǎ zhèxiē shū dàizǒu.
examples.english: You can take these books away.

examples.hanzi: 小偷把我的钱包带走了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu bǎ wǒ de qiánbāo dàizǒu le.
examples.english: The thief took my wallet away.
